headline: Broad network egress plus shared filesystem create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; no critical pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read/write files and uses stdin/stdout plus files passed on the command line, while aci can ingest and emit CRM/email/calendar content through APIs and MCP. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The shared filesystem and direct function-call/MCP patterns make this more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF aci writes untrusted external content into shared files or messages that Mentat later parses as instructions
IF Mentat reads files produced by aci without provenance checks
IF an MCP or filesystem bridge is used between the agents
mitigations: Add a provenance header to all inter-agent files/messages
Restrict Mentat to a dedicated input directory
Require manual review before Mentat acts on aci-generated text
Disable automatic parsing of CRM/email content as instructions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; Mentat reads selected files and writes diffs, so sensitive content can flow from shared files into model-provider requests or external APIs. The pair does not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default workflows even though the exact workspace sharing is not fully documented.
conditions: IF CRM, email, or support data from aci is placed in files Mentat opens
IF Mentat sends those file contents to its model provider
IF both agents operate under the same workspace or OAuth principal
mitigations: Keep aci and Mentat on separate workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before passing files to Mentat
Use a local-only model for Mentat when handling sensitive files
Rotate and scope API keys used by either agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem. aci supports multiple instances and broad network egress, so concurrent edits or state updates can collide on shared resources. Because both agents can act on mutable artifacts without documented locking, the default pair is unsafe for irreversible repo or workspace changes.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace
IF Mentat modifies git state while aci updates files or generated artifacts
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Serialize writes with a simple file lock
Require git status checks before each commit-like action
Limit aci to read-only operations during Mentat edits
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a built-in verification step. That creates a realistic cascade where incorrect facts or malformed edits propagate into downstream actions. The profiles do not show strong cross-checking, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes aci-generated text as authoritative task context
IF aci forwards Mentat-produced diffs or summaries into external systems
IF no human verification occurs between generation and action
mitigations: Require a human approval step before external actions
Compare outputs against source files before applying diffs
Use structured schemas for inter-agent handoff
Log and review all agent-to-agent transformations
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, calendar, support, and research data, while Mentat reads selected files and sends content to a configured model provider. If regulated or region-bound data is placed into the shared workflow, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR/SOC2 boundaries, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated customer data is processed by aci and then passed to Mentat's model provider
IF retention policies differ between the CRM/email system and the coding workflow
IF deletion or export requests must cover both agents' logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the coding workflow
Document retention settings for both agents
Use a DPA-approved model provider for Mentat
Minimize logging of prompts and diffs
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
